text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian President Mubarak and King Hassan examine memorandum of understanding on trade, investment and air and sea links.
- Crown Prince Mohamed, visiting Spain, says "current relations and progress made so far augur for even better ties".
- Jobless graduate attempts suicide out of despair.
- Police seize 1,300 kg (2,900 lb) of cannabis hidden in two cars in northern city of Nador.
- European Union Fisheries Commissioner Bonino expected for two-day visit to Morocco on May 26 to chair seminar on fisheries industries.
- Palestinian Authority Culture and Information Minister Rabbo says most important decisions concerning "Palestine" have been taken in Morocco.
- Tourism Minister M'hamedi says "prohibitive fares" of state-owned airline Royal Air Maroc deter tourists.
- Domestic and foreign debt weigh heavily on budget despite positive impact of privatisations and concession of water and electricity distribution to French firm Lyonnaise des Eaux.

- Mansour Kelada-Antoun, representative of World Bank's International Finance Corporation, tells la Nouvelle Tribune "international interest for investing in Morocco is real but there is need to give more scope of action to foreign investors including infrastructure, airlines and telecommunications".
